notes.hierarchy: Headlines lead clearly, but the fact strip and the sparse ask-cards compete weakly and dilute the reading order.
notes.typography: A clean sans with a good bold heading scale and comfortable line height, though generic and with awkward capitalisation.
notes.color: A restrained, coherent indigo palette with good contrast and purposeful accent use.
notes.layout: Varied sections (split hero, card grids, doctor band, list with sidebar headings), but the services pairing leaves big empty areas.
notes.spacing: Generally consistent rhythm, with misaligned baselines in the jump tiles and padded voids in the ask-cards.
notes.imagery: Relevant, warm photos fit the clinic well, though they are somewhat stock-like.
notes.mobile: Deliberately restacked with a centred hero and usable controls; the small two-column tile grid is the only weak spot.
notes.consistency: Header, footer, cards and colours are shared coherently across pages and breakpoints.
notes.polish: Clean pill buttons, accordions and footer, with a few rough spots in card fill and tile alignment.
notes.fit: Calm, trustworthy clinic tone and honest placeholders; the primary actions are limited by unknown details but navigation is clear.

strengths: Coherent indigo/lavender palette on an off-white base, with a dark footer that gives clear surface rhythm.
Consistent content width, rounded-card language and small-caps eyebrow labels across both pages.
Original, relevant clinic photography with consistent rounded crops.
Handles unknown details honestly with graceful placeholders and an urgent-care notice.
Mobile layouts restack sensibly, with readable text, a Menu button and full-width cards.
issues: Home services section on desktop: the 'You might ask' companion cards are equal height to the image cards but hold only two bullet lines, leaving large empty lavender areas with content floating mid-card.
Hero subcopy capitalises service names mid-sentence ('General consultations, Preventive-care visits'), which reads awkwardly; the footer repeats the same phrasing.
'Not sure where to start?' jump-link tiles have uneven label baselines: two-line titles sit higher than one-line titles, so the row looks misaligned.
Home hero on desktop leaves dead space above the headline. The fact strip below (Clinic/Where/Doctor) restates obvious info and dilutes hierarchy.
Contact page has no real contact action, which follows the brief, but the 'Find the clinic' CTA leads to a page that only says 'coming soon'.
On phone, the home jump-link tiles become a cramped two-column grid with heavy top rules.

notes.hierarchy: Each screen has a clear primary heading and next action, though some mid-page card sections compete slightly because many items share similar weight.
notes.typography: The type is readable, well scaled and consistent, but not especially distinctive and a few label/capitalisation choices feel mechanical.
notes.color: The restrained purple, lavender, white and dark footer palette is coherent and accessible-looking, with the accent generally used well.
notes.layout: The compositions are balanced and responsive, but some large card/list sections feel sparse or repetitive rather than fully custom-fit to the content.
notes.spacing: Alignment and spacing are mostly precise with a calm rhythm, though a few desktop sections leave noticeably loose gaps.
notes.imagery: Images are relevant, polished and well integrated overall, but they have a generic stock-clinic feel.
notes.mobile: The phone views appear deliberately composed with usable controls and readable text, although the expanded menu state is not visible in the screenshots.
notes.consistency: The pages share a coherent component system, palette, typography and footer treatment across desktop and mobile.
notes.polish: Buttons, cards, borders and footer are cleanly finished, with only minor roughness in repeated labels and some sparse section detailing.
notes.fit: The tone suits a calm general-care clinic and key information is easy to find while respecting the unknown contact details.

strengths: The main hero messages on both pages are clear, calm and immediately appropriate for a general-care clinic.
The purple and lavender visual system is cohesive, readable and consistently applied across cards, buttons, navigation and footer.
The site uses graceful placeholders for unknown address, phone and hours instead of inventing details.
Mobile layouts are comfortably reflowed with readable text, large controls and no obvious overflow.
The footer, navigation, emergency guidance and service links give visitors sensible next steps without adding a nonfunctional appointment form.
issues: The home service area uses large paired cards, especially the lavender 'You might ask' panels, with a lot of empty space on desktop.
Several secondary sections rely on similar card and list patterns, so the middle and lower home page can feel somewhat template-like despite being clean.
The contact page's desktop visit/FAQ area has very wide horizontal gaps, making the accordions feel a little isolated from their heading.
The photography is relevant and high quality, but it reads as generic clinic stock imagery and some crops feel more decorative than informative.
A few labels and phrases feel slightly awkward or over-styled, such as repeated title-case service names inside sentences and many small uppercase category labels.

notes.hierarchy: Focal points are immediately obvious, guiding the user naturally through the services and contact options.
notes.typography: The type system is robust, with deliberate scale and weight choices that ensure excellent readability.
notes.color: The restrained use of purple as an accent against soft gradients and white creates a trustworthy, clinical yet warm feel.
notes.layout: Compositions are varied—mixing cards, lists, and feature blocks—keeping the layout engaging without feeling cluttered.
notes.spacing: Margins and padding are mathematically consistent, creating a strong, invisible grid that holds the design together.
notes.imagery: Photography is high-quality, relevant, and cropped effectively to fit the rounded-corner aesthetic of the UI.
notes.mobile: The mobile experience feels native and intentional, with appropriately sized touch targets and stacked layouts.
notes.consistency: Components, colors, and typographic styles are applied with absolute uniformity across both pages.
notes.polish: Every detail, from the subtle border radii to the styling of the accordion icons, feels considered and finished.
notes.fit: The design perfectly captures the required tone and makes key actions like finding the clinic or learning about care frictionless.

strengths: Graceful and creative handling of missing contact information using well-designed placeholder text and layout.
Highly coherent visual language with a calming, professional color palette perfectly suited for a medical clinic.
Excellent typographic hierarchy and spacing rhythm that makes scanning and reading effortless on both desktop and mobile.
issues: No concrete visible issues exist; the design is executed to a professional studio standard, perfectly fulfilling the brief with exceptional polish and coherence across all breakpoints.

notes.hierarchy: Headlines and CTAs lead clearly on each screen, though the contact grid of repeated placeholders flattens emphasis.
notes.typography: Clear scale and eyebrow labels, but the serif headings read as a default system face.
notes.color: Soft, coherent palette with a restrained purple accent and good contrast.
notes.layout: Varied split, grid and band sections, with some unbalanced areas such as the clinician tile and unequal service cards.
notes.spacing: Generally consistent container and rhythm, with a few overly large gaps.
notes.imagery: The original flat illustration and icons fit the subject, but the clinician icon tile is weak.
notes.mobile: Deliberately stacked with full-width buttons and readable text; the clinician tile is not centred.
notes.consistency: Header, footer, cards and colours are shared coherently across both pages and breakpoints.
notes.polish: Clean overall, but the default-looking footer links and cramped icon caption detract.
notes.fit: Tone suits a calm clinic, and contact actions are prominent and honest about missing details.

strengths: A calm lavender, cream, sage and peach palette suits a general-care clinic, with the purple accent used consistently on CTAs.
The hero has a clear headline, supporting copy, primary and secondary CTAs, and an original illustrated room scene.
Placeholders are handled gracefully and honestly, with no fabricated hours, phone or address, and no fake booking form.
Alternating surface colours give a clear section rhythm, and the content width stays consistent across sections.
The phone layout stacks cleanly with full-width buttons, a labelled Menu button and comfortable text sizes.
Emergency guidance and visit-preparation content are useful and well placed.
issues: The serif display face looks like a system Times/Georgia fallback, so headings feel generic and slightly dated next to the Noto Sans body.
The clinician 'portrait' is a stethoscope icon tile whose 'Dr. Demo A' caption sits tight against the circle and looks cramped; on desktop the tile floats with excess space beside the text column.
The services grid on desktop has unequal card widths: the first card is wider and tinted while the other two are white.
The contact page's six placeholder cards are all 'To be confirmed', so a large grid area repeats the same italic text with little visual interest.
Some sections have uneven vertical spacing: large empty bands appear above the CTA band and above the 'Please note' disclaimer on the contact page.
The footer's bright underlined links look like browser defaults compared with the more refined components elsewhere.

notes.hierarchy: The main message and next actions are clear on each screen, though some repeated card sections have less distinct priority.
notes.typography: The serif headings and sans body create a polished, readable system with comfortable line lengths and mostly consistent scale.
notes.color: The lavender, cream, peach and dark-purple palette is coherent and calm, with the purple accent used effectively and with adequate contrast.
notes.layout: The compositions are balanced and responsive, but the repeated card grids and occasional sparse areas keep them from feeling fully bespoke.
notes.spacing: Alignment is strong and the rhythm is consistent overall, though some vertical gaps feel slightly overextended.
notes.imagery: The graphics fit the healthcare subject and integrate well, but they are relatively simple and somewhat generic.
notes.mobile: The phone views are comfortable and deliberately stacked, with readable text and buttons, though the generous spacing increases scrolling.
notes.consistency: The same components, colours, typography and footer treatment carry across both pages and breakpoints.
notes.polish: The site feels finished and clean, with good buttons and cards, but a few details such as footer links and placeholder-heavy cards are not quite studio-perfect.
notes.fit: The tone, copy and honest contact placeholders suit the fictional clinic brief very well and avoid nonfunctional booking or fabricated details.

strengths: The site handles unknown phone, address, hours, booking and reviews gracefully without inventing information.
The visual language is calm, coherent and appropriate for a general-care clinic.
Headings, calls to action and section labels create a clear reading order on both pages.
The mobile layouts are readable and intentionally stacked, with large tap targets and a visible menu control.
The two pages share a consistent type, colour, card, button and footer system.
issues: Several mid-page areas rely heavily on similar rounded cards, especially the services and contact-detail grids, so parts of the site feel a little template-like.
The illustrations and icons are clean but quite simple and generic; the clinician graphic in particular feels more like a placeholder than a fully expressive brand asset.
Some vertical spacing is very generous on desktop and mobile, which creates calmness but also pushes practical details farther down the page than necessary.
A few finishing details, such as the default-looking underlined footer links and very sparse placeholder cards, are less refined than the strongest parts of the design.

notes.hierarchy: The use of scale, color, and layout creates an unmistakable reading order and clear focal points on every screen.
notes.typography: The pairing of a refined serif for headings with a clean sans-serif for body text is highly readable and sets a premium tone.
notes.color: The soft purple and beige palette is calming and appropriate, with darker tones providing excellent contrast for text and interactive elements.
notes.layout: Sections are varied and well-balanced, using columns and cards effectively to organize complex information without feeling cluttered.
notes.spacing: There is a rigorous and consistent spacing system that gives the content room to breathe and establishes a clear rhythm.
notes.imagery: The custom vector illustrations are high-quality, fit the clinic's approachable tone, and are perfectly integrated into the layouts.
notes.mobile: While the visible mobile components are beautifully adapted, the apparent omission of key sections in the homepage flow slightly impacts the overall experience.
notes.consistency: The visual language is flawlessly maintained across all pages, components, and screen sizes.
notes.polish: The design is extremely refined overall, though minor details like text-based arrows and default link underlines offer slight room for improvement.
notes.fit: The design perfectly captures the required tone and handles the brief's constraints regarding missing information with elegance and clarity.

strengths: The color palette and typography establish a highly professional, calming, and trustworthy tone perfectly suited for a medical practice.
The requirement for 'graceful placeholders' is executed brilliantly, using styled cards that clearly communicate missing information without looking like errors.
Custom illustrations and a rigorous spacing system create a cohesive, premium visual language across all viewports.
issues: The mobile homepage screenshots omit the 'Preparing for a visit' and main CTA sections, creating an abrupt jump in the user journey.
The 'Full visit preparation ->' link uses a basic text arrow (hyphen and greater-than sign) rather than a polished vector icon.
Footer navigation links rely on default browser underlines that sit tight against the text, missing a final touch of typographic refinement.

note: Each site is scored on its own (absolute), from screenshots, with tool names hidden. Radial Pulse generates with an Anthropic model, so scores are also reported without the Anthropic judge.
